name: Teguima, 'llamada vulgarmente Opata'

catalog_quote: Del Accento. 21. No es menos necessaria la noticia de los Accentos, de lo q[ue] se ha dicho hablando de las letras, para la pronunciacion. y assi reduzgo los Accentos a tres. el Primero: es que se llama circumfloxo notado assi ^. el qual sirue para denotar la pronunciacion larga de la letra sobre quien se viere notado, y esto pronunciando con alguna fuerça. V.g. Jacûtui. sig.ca andar derrotado, y olbidarse. y lo mesmo es Naccûratui. olbidarse, 22. El segundo viene señalado con una C recostada assi ˘; y denota la sillaba breue V.g. Tepĭco. hazer almazigos. Hidagüăi. nacer. q[ue] tener vida. 23. El tercero viene formado de dos pu[n]tos assi ¨ y sirve para denotar que la vocal señalada se ha pronunciar como doble, dando mas espacio para la pronunciacion como si fueran dos, V.g. Vïhpi. que sig.ca Todavia falta. y aduiertase [fol. 7v] todo lo dicho por que de los accentos se varia el modo de hablar, por tener este lenguaje varios nombres, y berbos, que parecen sinonimos, y segun el espacio, o priessa con que se pronuncian tienen su significacion. Esto aduertido paso al Nombre. [Pimentel 1862: 409 §5: 'La diferencia de acento basta para que una voz cambie de significado. El P. Lombardo usa tres: el circunflejo (^) que denota pronunciación larga; otro (˘) breve; y el tercero, que se expresa con dos puntos (¨), indica que la letra se pronuncia duplicada; v. g., üi, traer, suena uui.']
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: No es menos necesaria la noticia de los Accentos [...] y assi reduzgo los Accentos a tres. el Primero es que se llama circumfloxo notado assi ^. el qual sirve para denotar la pronunciacion larga de la letra sobre quien se viere notado, y esto pronunciando con alguna fuerça. V.g. Jacûtui. sig.ca andar derrotado, y olbidarse [...] El segundo viene señalado con una C recostada assi ˘; y denota la sillaba breve [...] El tercero viene formado de dos puntos assi ¨ y sirve para denotar que la vocal señalada se ha pronunciar como doble [...] de los accentos se varia el modo de hablar [...] y segun el espacio, o priessa con que se pronuncian tienen su significacion.
new_statements.translation: Knowledge of the accents is no less necessary [...] and so I reduce the accents to three. The first is the one called circumflex, marked thus ^, which serves to mark the long pronunciation of the letter over which it is written, and this pronounced with some force, e.g. Jacûtui 'to wander lost, and to forget' [...] The second is marked with a reclining C thus ˘ and denotes the short syllable [...] The third is formed of two dots thus ¨ and serves to show that the marked vowel is to be pronounced as double [...] by the accents the manner of speaking varies [...] and according to the slowness or haste with which they are pronounced they have their meaning.
new_statements.citation: Lombardo, Natal. [ca. 1700]. Arte de la lengua teguima llamada vulgarmente opata. Manuscript, Newberry Library, Chicago, Ayer MS 1641 (manuscript version of the Arte printed México: Miguel de Ribera, 1702), 'Del Accento', §§21-23.
new_statements.locator: fol. 7r-7v (§§21-23 'Del Accento'), PDF pages 19-20 of the archive.org scan ayer_ms_1641; the same passage is paraphrased in Pimentel 1862, tomo 1, p. 409 §5 'Acentos' (1874 ed. p. 97).
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: LOCATOR/QUOTE: Opened (489 pp., archive.org ayer_ms_1641, Newberry VAULT Ayer MS 1641, 236 leaves, added 2026-03-20) and re-rendered pp. 18-21 myself plus the held PNGs. p. 19 = fol. 7r headed 'Del Accento' with numbered §§21-23; p. 20 = fol. 7v with the closing sentence and 'Libro Primero'. Reading the cursive page scan, the quoted passage is there: '§21 No es menos necessaria la noticia de los Accentos, de lo q[ue] se ha dicho hablando de las letras, para la pronunciacion. y assi reduzgo los Accentos a tres. el Primero: es que se llama circumfloxo notado assi ^. el qual sirve para denotar la pronunciacion larga de la letra sobre quien se viere notado, y esto pronunciando con alguna fuerça…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only primary statement is Lombardo's colonial 'accent' section: accent is a word-by-word diacritic notation of vowel quantity (long/short/doubled), the long vowel being pronounced 'with some force', and accent differences distinguish otherwise homophonous words. No rule for the position of stress is given anywhere in the section; stress proper (as opposed to length) is not isolated. Reading is therefore provisional: the source treats accent as lexically marked and contrastive, but it could equally be filed as unclear.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the section ends by warning that the language has many nouns and verbs that look synonymous and differ only by accent/tempo.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms of single words (nouns and verbs) in a missionary grammar of the pre-1702 language; the manuscript is a copy of the Arte, and Pimentel 1862:409 confirms the same three-way system in the printed edition. No modern first-hand description of stress was reachable (Shaul 1989 is print-only).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source is the Newberry Ayer MS 1641 manuscript of Lombardo's Arte (ca. 1700), describing the 17th/18th-century Teguima of the Sonora missions; Shaul's hh.bib entries call the same data 'Arivechi Opata'. Buckingham Smith 1861/1970 'Heve' (listed by Glottolog under opat1246) describes Eudeve (eude1234), not Teguima, and was set aside. No living-speaker data exist; all modern work re-analyzes Lombardo.

sources.citation: Lombardo, Natal. [ca. 1700]. Arte de la lengua teguima llamada vulgarm[en]te opata. Manuscript, Newberry Library, Ayer MS 1641 (236 leaves; manuscript version of the Arte printed México: Miguel de Ribera, 1702). archive.org item ayer_ms_1641.
sources.note: Section 'Del Accento' (fol. 7r-7v, §§21-23, pp. 19-20, read from the page scan): the 'accents' are reduced to three diacritics — circumflex = long pronunciation of the vowel 'pronunciando con alguna fuerça' (e.g. Jacûtui, Haccûratui), breve = short syllable (Tepĭco, Hidagüăi), diaeresis = doubled vowel (Vïhpi); accent differences change meaning between apparent synonyms. It is a quantity(+force) notation marked word by word; no rule for where accent falls.
Consonant/vowel inventories (five short/long vowels) with no stress statement; bibliography lists Shaul 1983, 1989, 1990, 2014, de Wolf 2001, Lombardo 1702, Miller 1983, Lionnet 1979.

tone.quote: vowel may be discussed under the rubric of syllable shape,4 but of more importance are stress patterns, seen in Table 2. Toward the south, stress falls on the second syllable or a suffix. This occurs in Tr and Gu (exception: stress on second syllables in verb roots). This usually occurs in Op, Eu and Tu. Stress is always initial in Ca. However, Op and Eu may have initial stress. Heath (1977) points out that stress in UA may have been variable with respect to verb morphology.
tone.locator: p. 100 ('Vowels and Stress Patterns', running from the foot of p. 99), with Table 2 'Stress Patterns' on p. 104 and transcription note 2 on p. 102 ('vowel length is indicated by a raised dot [V·], an acute accent indicates stress')
tone.summary: No tone statement. Prosody treated only as stress placement and vowel length: Opata (with Eudeve, Tubar) usually has stress on the second syllable or a suffix, but Opata and Eudeve may also show initial stress, an innovation Shaul groups with Cahitan initial stress.
